data:
Welcome to the AWS ClinicalCompass documentation. This guide covers the business context, technical architecture, and deployment instructions for the clinical guidelines AI assistant.
Business ContextWhy clinical guidelines navigation needs AI assistance How It WorksAgentic retrieval, reasoning, and conflict resolution ArchitectureServerless components and data flow InstallationDeploy ClinicalCompass in your AWS account DevelopmentDay-to-day workflows for agents, Lambda, and KBs AgentsMulti-agent architecture and conflict resolution ObservabilityMonitoring, tracing, and troubleshooting

ClinicalCompass uses a supervisor pattern where a central orchestrator coordinates three specialised agents that run in parallel. Each agent has a single responsibility and queries its own knowledge base.
data.conflict-resolution#Conflict Resolution:
When agents return contradictory recommendations, the supervisor applies precedence rules:
Local Regulatory > National > International Example conflict:
ACR (International): “Gadolinium contrast can be used with caution for eGFR 30-44” HAS France (Local): “Gadolinium contrast should be avoided for eGFR <45” Resolution: HAS France takes precedence — local protocols are more conservative for patient safety and legal compliance Rationale for local precedence:
Legal compliance in local jurisdiction Patient safety (local protocols are often more conservative) Regulatory requirements that clinicians must follow
data.data-sources#Data sources: knowledge-bases/data/ ├── ehr/ # Patient records ├── guidelines/ # International clinical guidelines └── regulatory/ # Local regulatory protocols
data.global-guidelines-agent#Global Guideline:
Consults international clinical guideline knowledge bases.
Tool: query_guidelines(clinical_scenario, guideline_sources)
Knowledge Base: Global Guidelines KB
ACR (American College of Radiology) ESUR (European Society of Urogenital Radiology) NICE (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence) WHO guidelines Example query:
query_guidelines( clinical_scenario="MRI with contrast for patient with reduced kidney function", guideline_sources=["ACR", "ESUR", "NICE"] ) Returns: JSON with source, recommendation text, evidence level, confidence score, and citation.
data.knowledge-bases#Knowledge Bases:
All three KBs use the same configuration:
Embedding model: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 Chunking: 512 tokens, 20% overlap Vector store: OpenSearch Serverless Retrieval: Semantic search via Bedrock Knowledge Bases
data.local-regulatory-agent#Local Regulatory:
Checks national and local regulatory protocols that may override international guidelines.
Tool: query_regulatory_protocols(clinical_scenario, jurisdiction, protocol_sources)
Knowledge Base: Local Regulatory KB
HAS France (Haute Autorité de Santé) protocols NHS local trust policies Regional SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) Formulary restrictions Example query:
query_regulatory_protocols( clinical_scenario="MRI with contrast for patient with reduced kidney function", jurisdiction="France", protocol_sources=["HAS"] ) Returns: JSON with source, requirement text, mandatory/recommended flag, confidence score, and citation.
data.patient-context-agent#Patient Context Ag:
Retrieves patient-specific data from the EHR knowledge base.
Tool: query_ehr(patient_id, query_context)
Knowledge Base: EHR KB
Patient demographics Lab results (eGFR, creatinine, etc.) Current medications Allergies Active conditions Example query:
query_ehr( patient_id="patient_001", query_context="kidney function for contrast imaging" ) Returns: Structured JSON with relevant patient data, labs, medications, allergies, and conditions.
data.performance#Performance: Full multi-agent workflow: 30-40 seconds All three specialised agents execute in parallel Hot storage retrieval (decision traces): <200ms Individual KB query: 2-5 seconds
data.session-management#Session Management: Multi-turn conversations use session_id for context continuity Patient data is cached in AgentCore short-term memory within a session Follow-up questions reference previous context without re-querying Session timeout: 30 minutes of inactivity
data.supervisor-agent#Supervisor Agent:
The orchestrator that manages the entire clinical decision workflow.
Responsibilities:
Parse clinical queries and extract entities (patient demographics, symptoms, intended action) Coordinate parallel agent execution Detect conflicts between guideline recommendations Apply precedence rules (local > national > international) Generate safety alerts and alternatives Produce a final recommendation with citations Tools:
Tool Purpose detect_conflicts Identifies disagreements between agent responses apply_precedence_rules Resolves conflicts using local > national > international hierarchy generate_safety_alerts Analyses contraindications and risks search_alternatives Finds clinically equivalent safer options synthesize_recommendation Produces the final cited recommendation Key behaviours:
No intermediate narration between tool calls — only the final recommendation is surfaced Multi-turn conversations supported via session memory Patient data cached within sessions to avoid redundant EHR queries All overridden recommendations documented for audit trail

data: AWS ClinicalCompass is built on a serverless architecture using AWS managed services.
data.ai-processing-engine#AI Processing Engin:
The agentic system runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore:
Foundation model: Claude Sonnet via Amazon Bedrock Supervisor Agent orchestrates three specialised agents in parallel AgentCore Memory (STM) maintains session context for multi-turn conversations Decision traces stored for audit compliance See Agents for detailed agent architecture.
data.data-ingestion-pipelines#Data Ingestion: Three separate ingestion paths feed the knowledge bases and DynamoDB:
data.frontend#Frontend:
A vanilla JavaScript application served via CloudFront, using the AG-UI protocol for real-time streaming of agent events to the browser:
Patient Selector — dropdown populated from DynamoDB via HTTP API Guideline Selector — choose which guideline sources to consult Citation Panel — click-through links to source documents Decision Trail — expandable reasoning trace with conflict resolution details
data.guidelines-pipeline#Guidelines Pipeline: S3 (guidelines) → Lambda (Guideline Ingestion) → DynamoDB (guideline-registry) + KB sync Triggered by S3 upload events Stores lightweight metadata in DynamoDB (source name, status) for the UI dropdown Full content goes to the Guidelines Knowledge Base for RAG
data.infrastructure-as-code#Infrastructure as:
The entire stack is deployed via AWS CDK (TypeScript):
DynamoDB tables (connections, patient-index, guideline-registry) 10 Lambda functions (WebSocket handlers, ingestion, API, keep-alive) WebSocket + HTTP API Gateways S3 buckets (frontend, EHR data, guidelines, regulatory, KB data x3) CloudFront distribution + OAC OpenSearch Serverless collections AWS HealthLake FHIR datastore (patient data in FHIR R4 format) Cognito User Pool SSM Parameter Store (resource IDs, ARNs, endpoints) CloudWatch Events (AgentCore keep-alive every 5 min)
data.knowledge-base-layer#Knowledge Base Laye:
Three Bedrock Knowledge Bases provide semantic retrieval:
Knowledge Base Content Agent EHR Patient demographics, labs, medications, allergies Patient Context Agent Guidelines ACR, ESUR, NICE, WHO clinical guidelines Global Guidelines Agent Regulatory HAS France, NHS local trust protocols, SOPs Local Regulatory Agent All KBs use:
Embedding: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 Chunking: 512 tokens, 20% overlap Vector store: OpenSearch Serverless
data.patient-ehr-pipeline#Patient (EHR) Pipel: S3 (ehr-data) → Lambda (EHR Ingestion) → HealthLake (FHIR R4) + DynamoDB (patient-index) + KB sync Triggered by S3 upload events Transforms patient JSON to FHIR R4 format and stores in AWS HealthLake Computes section hashes for differential detection (only changed sections re-processed) Stores structured records in DynamoDB for direct lookups (UI Patient Selector) Syncs to EHR Knowledge Base for RAG retrieval (semantic search by agents)
data.real-time-query-path#Real-Time Query Pat:
The primary interaction path for clinicians uses WebSocket for streaming responses:
CloudFront serves the static frontend from S3 (OAC-secured) WebSocket API Gateway handles real-time bidirectional communication 6 Lambda handlers manage connection lifecycle and query routing AgentCore Runtime hosts the multi-agent system that processes clinical queries
data.regulatory-pipeline#Regulatory Pipeline: S3 (local-regulatory) → KB ingestion job (direct sync) No Lambda intermediary — documents sync directly to the Regulatory KB Always consulted by the Local Regulatory Agent (no user selection needed)
data.rest-api#REST API:
An HTTP API Gateway provides structured data endpoints for the frontend UI:
Endpoint Purpose GET /patients List patients for the Patient Selector dropdown GET /patients/{id} Retrieve specific patient context GET /guidelines List available guideline sources for the Guideline Selector These endpoints read directly from DynamoDB (patient-index and guideline-registry tables), populated by the ingestion pipelines.
data.security-and-compliance#Security and Com: Authentication: Amazon Cognito (USER_PASSWORD_AUTH + USER_SRP_AUTH) Frontend hosting: CloudFront with Origin Access Control (OAC) to S3 Data encryption: At rest (S3 SSE, DynamoDB encryption, OpenSearch encryption) and in transit (TLS) Network: All service-to-service communication via AWS internal endpoints Observability: ADOT tracing with clinical decision audit trail
data.system-overview#System Overview: The system has three major layers: a real-time query path (WebSocket), a REST API for structured data, and data ingestion pipelines that feed the knowledge bases.

data.agentic-guideline-navigation#Agentic gui: An AI agent that understands the structure and hierarchy of clinical guidelines, retrieving from the relevant sources based on the clinical question.
data.benefits#Benefits: Time savings: Reduces the effort of searching across multiple guideline databases to a single natural language query. Consistency: Ensures clinicians access the most current, locally-relevant guidance regardless of which source it originates from. Completeness: Surfaces all relevant layers of guidance (national, regional, local) rather than relying on a single source. Workforce productivity: Frees clinical time for direct patient care rather than administrative searching.
data.evidence-based-citations#Evidence-based: Every response includes citations to source documents, enabling clinicians to verify recommendations and maintain clinical accountability.
data.getting-started#Getting Started: Ready to deploy ClinicalCompass in your environment? Follow our installation guide to get started.
data.human-in-the-loop-design#Human-in-the-lo: ClinicalCompass assists clinical decision-making - it does not replace it. All outputs are clearly presented as guideline summaries requiring clinical judgement.
data.multi-source-aggregation#Multi-source ag: Retrieves and reasons across national guidelines, local trust policies, and formulary data to provide a unified, contextualised answer.
data.natural-language-interaction#Natural lan: Clinicians can ask questions in plain clinical language rather than constructing keyword searches across multiple databases.
data.our-solution#Our Solution: AWS ClinicalCompass addresses these challenges through:
data.the-challenge#The Challenge:
Healthcare professionals face significant challenges when navigating clinical guidelines:
Layered complexity: Guidelines exist at multiple levels - national (NICE, SIGN, BNF), regional (NHS Trust/ICB), and local (formulary, commercial agreements). A single clinical question may require consulting guidance from several sources. Volume: NICE alone publishes over 2,000 guidelines, quality standards, and technology appraisals. Each NHS Trust adds local policies on top. Geographic variation: Clinical pathways vary by region. The same condition may be managed differently depending on local funding decisions, available services, and formulary restrictions. Time pressure: Clinicians need answers at the point of care, often during consultations, with limited time to search across multiple sources. Currency: Guidelines are regularly updated. Keeping track of changes across multiple sources is a significant administrative burden. Current processes rely on clinicians manually searching guideline databases, reading lengthy PDF documents, and cross-referencing multiple sources.
data.what-are-clinical-guidelines#What are Cl: Clinical guidelines are evidence-based recommendations that help clinicians make decisions about patient care in specific clinical circumstances. They are produced by national bodies (e.g., NICE in England/Wales), professional societies, and individual healthcare organisations.

data: Day-to-day workflows for modifying agents, updating infrastructure, and managing knowledge bases.
data.cicd-integration#CI/CD Integration:
The build script supports versioned tags for pipeline use:
# Tag with commit SHA python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py --tag $CI_COMMIT_SHA # Build only (no push) python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py --no-push
data.ehr-pipeline#EHR Pipeline: # Upload patient data to trigger ingestion aws s3 cp knowledge-bases/data/ehr/patient_001_jean_pierre_dubois.json \ s3://clinicalcompass-ehr-data-/ \ --profile --region us-east-1 # Verify DynamoDB was populated aws dynamodb scan --table-name clinicalcompass-patient-index \ --profile --region us-east-1 --query 'Count' # Verify via REST API curl $(aws ssm get-parameter --name /clinicalcompass/http-api-endpoint \ --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text)/patients
data.guidelines-pipeline#Guidelines Pipeline: # Upload a guideline document aws s3 cp knowledge-bases/data/guidelines/acr_contrast_manual_2024.md \ s3://clinicalcompass-guidelines-/ \ --profile --region us-east-1 # Check guideline registry aws dynamodb scan --table-name clinicalcompass-guideline-registry \ --profile --region us-east-1 \ --query 'Items[*].{source:source_name.S,status:status.S}' --output table
data.knowledge-base-vectorisation#Knowledge B: # Test RAG retrieval (proof vectorisation works) aws bedrock-agent-runtime retrieve \ --knowledge-base-id \ --retrieval-query '{"text": "patient with renal impairment eGFR 32"}' \ --profile --region us-east-1 \ --query 'retrievalResults[0].content.text' --output text
data.post-cdk-script-options#Post-CDK Script:
The post_cdk_setup.py script supports selective execution:
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py # full setup python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-kb # skip Knowledge Base creation python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-runtime # skip AgentCore Runtime python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-memory # skip Memory creation python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-data # skip KB data upload python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-config # skip config file updates
data.project-structure#Project Structure: aws-clinicalcompanion/ ├── backend/ │ ├── agents/ # Multi-agent system │ │ ├── supervisor_agent.py │ │ ├── patient_context_agent.py │ │ ├── global_guidelines_agent.py │ │ └── local_regulatory_agent.py │ ├── utils/ # Shared utilities │ │ ├── session_manager.py │ │ ├── memory_utils.py │ │ ├── agui_emitter.py │ │ ├── metadata_extractor.py │ │ ├── clinical_observability.py │ │ └── kb_config.py │ ├── lambda/websocket/ # 5 Lambda handlers │ ├── app.py # AgentCore container entry point │ └── requirements.txt ├── frontend/ │ ├── css/ # Styles (agui, panel, auth) │ ├── js/ # App logic + auth │ └── index.html ├── infra/ # CDK infrastructure (TypeScript) │ ├── lib/ │ └── bin/app.ts ├── knowledge-bases/ │ ├── data/ # Clinical data (EHR, guidelines, regulatory) │ └── upload_data.py ├── deployment/ │ ├── scripts/ # Deployment and setup scripts │ └── config.py # Centralised configuration └── tests/ # Integration and unit tests
data.running-tests#Running Tests: # Backend unit tests (first time: pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt) cd backend && python -m pytest -q # CDK security assertion tests cd infra && npx jest To check a deployed stack end to end, sign in through the CloudFront URL and run a query. The WebSocket API requires a Cognito access token, so unauthenticated tools such as a plain wscat connection are rejected with 401.
data.running-the-frontend-locally#Running the:
cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080 # Open http://localhost:8080 Test query (patient 001, Jean-Pierre Dubois):
“68-year-old male with eGFR 32, needs MRI with gadolinium contrast”
data.updating-backend-agents#Updating Backend:
When you modify code in backend/agents/ or backend/utils/:
python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py This rebuilds the Docker image and pushes it to ECR. If the clinicalcompass runtime already exists, the script also updates it to the newly pushed image and waits for it to return to READY. During a fresh deploy, no runtime exists yet, so the script just builds and pushes the image.
For faster iteration during development:
bash deployment/scripts/quick_update_agentcore.sh
data.updating-infrastructure#Updating Infrast:
When you modify the CDK stack (new resources, policy changes):
cd infra npx cdk diff # preview changes npx cdk deploy # apply
data.updating-knowledge-base-data#Updating Kn:
When you add or modify clinical data in knowledge-bases/data/:
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-runtime --skip-memory This re-uploads data to S3 and triggers a KB sync without touching the runtime or memory configuration.
data.updating-lambda-handlers#Updating Lambda:
When you modify code in backend/lambda/websocket/:
cd infra && npx cdk deploy CDK detects the code change and updates only the affected Lambda functions.
data.updating-the-frontend#Updating the Front:
When you modify frontend HTML, JS, or CSS:
python deployment/scripts/deploy_frontend.py This regenerates config.js, uploads all files to S3, and invalidates the CloudFront cache. Changes are live in 1-2 minutes.
For local development (after post_cdk_setup.py has generated config.js):
cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080

data.citation-and-traceability#Citation and t: Every statement in a response links back to a specific section of a source document. Clinicians can click through to read the full guideline context.
data.conflict-resolution#Conflict resolution: When guidelines from different sources provide different recommendations, ClinicalCompass identifies the conflict and presents both positions with context on which takes precedence in the local setting.
data.guideline-hierarchy-awareness#Guideline: ClinicalCompass understands that clinical guidelines operate in layers. National guidance provides the baseline, but local trust policies, formulary decisions, and regional pathways may modify recommendations. The system surfaces all relevant layers.
data.overview#Overview: AWS ClinicalCompass uses an agentic AI architecture to process clinical queries through multiple stages: understanding the clinical context, retrieving relevant guidelines from multiple sources, resolving conflicts between them, and presenting a cited response.
data.query-processing#Query Processing:
Patient and guideline selection - The clinician selects a patient from the Patient Selector (populated from DynamoDB via REST API) and optionally filters guideline sources via the Guideline Selector.
Clinical context understanding - The agent interprets the clinical question, identifying the condition, patient context, and type of guidance needed (diagnostic, treatment, referral, prescribing).
Source identification - Based on the query and selected guidelines, the agent determines which knowledge bases are relevant (e.g., NICE for national guidance, local trust formulary for prescribing decisions).
Parallel retrieval - Three specialised agents execute simultaneously: Patient Context Agent queries EHR data, Global Guidelines Agent consults international sources, Local Regulatory Agent checks jurisdiction-specific protocols.
Conflict detection and resolution - The supervisor identifies disagreements between sources and applies precedence rules (local > national > international) to resolve them.
Response generation - The supervisor produces a structured response with clear citations, confidence indicators, safety alerts, alternatives ranked by safety profile, and links to source documents.

data: Deploy ClinicalCompass in your AWS account. The system uses AWS CDK for infrastructure provisioning and a post-deploy script for runtime configuration.
data.authentication#Authentication:
CDK deploys a Cognito User Pool (clinicalcompass-users) with:
An app client configured for browser use (no client secret) USER_PASSWORD_AUTH and USER_SRP_AUTH flows enabled Create login users after deployment with the Cognito admin CLI:
USER_POOL_ID=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \ --stack-name ClinicalCompassStack \ --region us-east-1 \ --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='CognitoUserPoolId'].OutputValue" \ --output text) aws cognito-idp admin-create-user \ --user-pool-id "$USER_POOL_ID" \ --username doctor \ --temporary-password '' \ --message-action SUPPRESS \ --region us-east-1 aws cognito-idp admin-set-user-password \ --user-pool-id "$USER_POOL_ID" \ --username doctor \ --password '' \ --permanent \ --region us-east-1 Choose a password that satisfies the pool policy: at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and a digit. The frontend authenticates directly via the Cognito InitiateAuth API. Tokens are stored in sessionStorage (cleared on tab close). No external SDK required.
data.cdk-managed-resources-incremental-deploy: Resource Purpose Cognito User Pool + App Client Authentication DynamoDB tables Connections, patient-index, guideline-registry ECR repository AgentCore container images IAM roles and policies AgentCore, Lambda, KB access 10 Lambda functions WebSocket handlers, EHR/guideline ingestion, patient/guideline APIs, keep-alive WebSocket API Gateway Real-time agent communication HTTP API Gateway REST endpoints (/patients, /guidelines) S3 buckets Frontend static files, EHR data, guidelines, regulatory, KB data x3 CloudFront + OAC HTTPS frontend hosting from S3 OpenSearch Serverless Vector search for KB retrieval SSM Parameter Store Resource IDs, ARNs, endpoints, frontend hosting config CloudWatch Events AgentCore keep-alive (every 5 min)
data.configuration#Configuration:
deployment/config.py holds only your AWS profile, region, and account ID (plus the ECR repository name). Everything else is discovered at run time from the CloudFormation stack outputs and SSM Parameter Store (runtime ARN, memory ID). post_cdk_setup.py also writes:
frontend/config.js - Cognito + WebSocket endpoint knowledge-bases/knowledge_base_ids.json - KB identifiers Config files are gitignored. Only *.example.* templates are committed.
data.environment-variables#Environment Variab: Variable Description Default AWS_REGION AWS region us-east-1 BEDROCK_MODEL_ID Bedrock model us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 BEDROCK_TEMPERATURE Model temperature 0 STM_MEMORY_ID Short-term memory ID Read from SSM EHR_KB_ID EHR Knowledge Base ID Read from SSM GUIDELINES_KB_ID Guidelines KB ID Read from SSM REGULATORY_KB_ID Regulatory KB ID Read from SSM
data.full-teardown#Full Teardown:
python deployment/scripts/cleanup_all.py S3 buckets and the ECR repository have RETAIN removal policy and won’t be deleted by cdk destroy alone. The cleanup script handles them.
AWS Bedrock may still leave deleted Knowledge Base names behind in DELETE_UNSUCCESSFUL. A subsequent deploy is still safe because post_cdk_setup.py detects those stale names and falls back to a reusable alternate Knowledge Base name when needed.
data.prerequisites#Prerequisites: AWS CLI v2, configured (aws configure). Use a recent version that includes the AgentCore commands: aws bedrock-agentcore-control help must work Node.js 18+ and npm Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended) Docker running, with buildx (Docker Desktop includes it; with Colima, brew install docker-buildx and link it into ~/.docker/cli-plugins/). AgentCore Runtime only runs linux/arm64 images; on an x86 Linux machine or CI runner, enable arm64 emulation once: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64 AWS CDK: npm install -g aws-cdk Access to Amazon Bedrock foundation models (Claude Sonnet) # Install Python dependencies pip install boto3 opensearch-py requests-aws4auth pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
data.script-managed-resources-runtime-operati: Script Purpose post_cdk_setup.py HealthLake, OpenSearch indices, Bedrock KBs, AgentCore Memory, AgentCore Runtime, data upload, config updates build_and_push_image.py Docker build and push to ECR; refresh existing AgentCore runtime when present deploy_frontend.py Generate config.js, upload to S3, invalidate CloudFront cleanup_all.py Full teardown of all resources including orphans
data.step-1-create-deployment-config#Step 1::
cp deployment/config.example.py deployment/config.py Edit deployment/config.py and set:
AWS_PROFILE - your named AWS CLI profile AWS_REGION - target region (default: us-east-1) AWS_ACCOUNT_ID - your 12-digit account ID
data.step-2-deploy-infrastructure#Step 2: Dep:
cd infra npm install npx cdk bootstrap # first time only npx cdk deploy --require-approval never Validate: the WebSocket API is up and rejects unauthenticated connections.
npx wscat -c wss://.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/production # Expected: error: Unexpected server response: 401
data.step-3-build-and-push-the-agent-containe:
Requires Docker running with buildx (Docker Desktop, or colima start with the buildx plugin). The script always builds a linux/arm64 image, the only architecture AgentCore Runtime runs, and pushes it straight to ECR.
cd .. python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py Validate:
aws ecr describe-images --repository-name bedrock-agentcore-clinicalcompass \ --profile --region us-east-1 \ --query 'imageDetails[0].imageTags' Common issues:
Docker: NOT RUNNING - Start Docker Desktop or run colima start docker buildx is required - Install the buildx plugin (see Prerequisites) Runtime rejects the image as the wrong architecture - Make sure you use this script (it builds linux/arm64), not a plain docker build no basic auth credentials - Remove credsStore from ~/.docker/config.json denied: Your authorization token has expired - Re-run the script (it re-authenticates)
data.step-4-complete-setup-healthlake-kbs-mem:
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py This script:
Creates HealthLake FHIR datastore (if configured) Creates OpenSearch indices Creates Bedrock Knowledge Bases Creates the AgentCore Runtime Provisions short-term memory Uploads clinical data to KBs Updates frontend/config.js and knowledge-bases/knowledge_base_ids.json Validate:
aws bedrock-agentcore-control list-agent-runtimes \ --profile --region us-east-1 \ --query 'agentRuntimes[?agentRuntimeName==`clinicalcompass`].{name:agentRuntimeName,status:status}' Common issues:
opensearch-py and requests-aws4auth required - Install them, then re-run with --skip-runtime --skip-memory --skip-config Collection status: CREATING - OpenSearch collections take 2-5 min after CDK deploy. Wait and re-run. Failed to create runtime - Check Docker image was pushed (Step 3) and IAM role exists.
data.step-5-deploy-frontend-to-cloudfront#Ste:
python deployment/scripts/deploy_frontend.py This generates config.js, uploads all frontend files to S3, and invalidates the CloudFront cache. Access via the CloudFront URL printed at the end.
Create a Cognito user with the post-deploy CLI commands in the Authentication section, then log in with that username and password.
For local development, you can also serve the frontend directly after step 4 (which generates config.js):
cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080 # Open http://localhost:8080

data: ClinicalCompass uses AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) for tracing, with custom clinical spans for healthcare-specific events.
data.agentcore-production#AgentCore (Producti:
Observability is configured in .bedrock_agentcore.yaml:
observability: enabled: true Custom clinical spans require an additional environment variable:
# In backend/app.py import os os.environ['AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED'] = 'true'
data.cloudwatch-logs-cli#CloudWatch Logs (CLI: # View recent application logs aws logs tail \ /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/clinicalcompass-DEFAULT \ --since 10m --region us-east-1 # Follow logs in real-time aws logs tail \ /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/clinicalcompass-DEFAULT \ --follow --region us-east-1
data.cloudwatch-logs-insights-queries#CloudWa:
Find all sessions:
fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /session/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 100 Find custom clinical spans:
fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /clinical\./ | sort @timestamp desc Find errors:
fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ or @message like /Exception/ | sort @timestamp desc Track a specific session:
fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like // | sort @timestamp asc
data.common-log-messages#Common log messages: Message Meaning Created session: New session started Stored session data Memory write successful Streaming Supervisor Agent response Agent invocation in progress AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED: true Custom spans active Failed to export span batch code: 403 Trace export rejected: CloudWatch Transaction Search not enabled, or X-Ray permissions missing from the AgentCore role
data.custom-clinical-spans#Custom Clinical Sp:
The backend/utils/clinical_observability.py module provides span helpers:
from clinical_observability import ( record_conflict_detection, record_precedence_rule_application, record_recommendation_generation, record_agent_coordination, clinical_span, ) # Conflict detection record_conflict_detection(session_id, conflicts, patient_id) # Precedence rule application record_precedence_rule_application( session_id=session_id, conflict="Contrast use for eGFR 32", chosen_guideline="HAS France", overridden_guideline="ACR International", rationale="Local regulatory requirements take precedence", patient_id=patient_id ) # Recommendation generation record_recommendation_generation(session_id, recommendation, patient_id) # Agent coordination timing record_agent_coordination( session_id=session_id, agent_name="patient_context", duration_ms=1500, success=True, patient_id=patient_id ) # Custom spans with clinical_span("custom.operation", session_id=session_id) as span: span.set_attribute("custom.attribute", "value")
data.dashboard-not-showing-data#Dashboard not: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search - AWS Console → CloudWatch → Settings → Enable Transaction Search X-Ray permissions are included in the CDK stack: the AgentCore role can write traces (xray:PutTraceSegments, PutTelemetryRecords, GetSamplingRules, GetSamplingTargets) and bedrock-agentcore metrics. If you still see Failed to export span batch code: 403, check that Transaction Search (step 1) is enabled. Run a test query and wait 1-2 minutes
data.dual-storage-strategy#Dual Storage Strat:
Clinical decision traces use two storage tiers:
Tier Technology Latency Retention Use Case Hot AgentCore Memory <100ms 24-48h UI “View Full Reasoning” button Cold CloudWatch Logs (OTEL) 5-10s 90 days+ Audit, compliance, forensics The hot tier stores a structured JSON decision trace written at the end of each recommendation. The cold tier receives complete OTEL spans automatically.
data.genai-observability-dashboard#GenAI Obse: Open CloudWatch Console Navigate to GenAI Observability → Bedrock AgentCore → Agents Select clinicalcompass View sessions, traces, and metrics
data.local-development#Local Development: export AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true export OTEL_PYTHON_DISTRO=aws_distro export OTEL_PYTHON_CONFIGURATOR=aws_configurator export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf export OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=clinical-compass
data.logging-scripts#Logging scripts: # AgentCore runtime logs (runtime ID is read from SSM, so it always matches the deployed runtime) python deployment/scripts/check_agentcore_logs.py --minutes 30 # Lambda logs, e.g. the WebSocket query handler aws logs tail /aws/lambda/clinicalcompass-ws-query --since 30m --follow --region us-east-1
data.what-gets-instrumented#What Gets Instrum:
AgentCore provides automatic observability:
All agent invocations are traced Tool calls logged with inputs/outputs Errors and exceptions captured Session context preserved across invocations Custom clinical spans add healthcare-specific signals:
Conflict detection - when guidelines disagree Precedence rule application - how conflicts are resolved Recommendation generation - final clinical output Agent coordination - per-agent timing and success
